properties.chose: @ajs, 2026-10-10: "Reopen: host hands reflow2 the readable set." The trusted gateway passes _meta["reflow2/readable_graph_ids"] (defined beside WRITES_FOR_META) on EVERY call, reads included — today it sends _meta only on writes (engine-api.ts:184-225) — and reflow2's resolver (ReflowService::other_design) refuses a graph_id not in that list, naming it, and refuses every cross-design read when no trusted gateway or bearer caller is present (a bare registry server never reaches another design by graph_id). reflow2 still has no identity system of its own: it trusts the host's list exactly as it already trusts writes_for, so reason 1 of the 2026-08-12 ruling ("reflow2 authenticates nothing") stands as narrowed on 2026-09-28. What changes is only this: for the cross-design primitive layer, isolation is no longer a property of what is under the root alone, because on flo2.io one root holds every tenant. Listing within a root stays unfiltered; a session bound to one design still cannot ADDRESS another by path (req:a-session-cannot-address-another-design holds). REJECTED: the gateway doing the join by shipping B's 9-16 MB export inline on every call (keeps reflow2 identity-free but cannot carry the on-demand view and costs the export each time); one root per tenant (what the original ruling assumed; flo2.io does not deploy that way and the memory measurement of 2026-10-10 says one process per tenant does not fit the droplet). properties.decision:
RE-OPENS dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary ("The registry ROOT is the tenant boundary — listing stays unfiltered, and reflow2 still authenticates nothing"), which stays accepted and untouched until this closes (dec:reopen-supersedes).

WHY: The 2026-08-12 ruling bounds isolation by WHAT IS THERE under one root and refuses any per-caller check. On 2026-10-10 Anthony kept req:every-cross-design-operation-takes-its-other-designs-by-graph-id-under-the-hosts-read-filter and the on-demand view requirement: a call bound to design A reads design B by graph_id through the registry. On flo2.io every tenant shares one root (engine-api.ts:11-12), so with the root as the only boundary any member of A could read any design on the droplet; the survey (f792e88dc) found no identity reaches a read today (the gateway sends _meta only on writes). The ruling must be re-asked for the cross-design case before step 3 of the build plan (the resolver's authorisation) is written. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-10 — a cross-design read by graph_id is bounded by the READABLE SET the trusted host hands reflow2 on every call (reads as well as writes), enforced by reflow2; the root stays the tenant boundary for everything else, and reflow2 still issues no identity
